entries.note: Aloulou 2015 (DOI resolves) conclusion sentence verbatim in abstract; untested opener 2015. Adrulipase alfa (YLLIP2/MS1819) is a listed member, oral; unselected EPI correct.
10-K R7 holds the 2.2 g/d, mean +21.8% quote. NCT03481803 first posted 2018-03-29 (CP), no results. Adrulipase alfa oral MS1819-SD, unselected; same/2018 unchanged.
In-vitro equivalence sentence verbatim in abstract; 10-K says 2.2 g/d was an FDA-agreed bridging dose, not a model target, so untested/no_prediction holds. Adrulipase alfa, oral, unselected.
Abstract conclusion verbatim: minipig CFA on YLLIP2 similar to 1.2 g pancreatin; untested opener 2015. Adrulipase alfa, oral, unselected correct.

Registry primary CFA 55.6 vs 86.2 (results 2022-06-06) sets contra. 31 Mar 2021 release: 'majority did not' reach non-inferiority; Sep 2019 release called OPTION positive, so 2021 is earliest. Judgement prose still says 2022.
IND-clearance sentence verbatim in 10-K R7; no published MS1819 toxicology found; untested/unpublished 2017 proxy stands. Adrulipase alfa, oral, unselected correct.
Suzuki 1997 (DOI resolves) abstract conclusion verbatim; B. plantarii lipase became burlulipase. Untested opener 1997; burlulipase, oral, unselected CF-EPI correct.
Heubi 2016 abstract quote verbatim: CFA 72.7% vs 53.8% placebo; NCT01710644 posted 2012-10-19, burlulipase oral solution vs placebo. Same 2016, oral, unselected stands.

missing: OPTION 2 topline press release, 31 Mar 2021 (https://firstwordpharma.com/story/5263483): 'OPTION 2 did not consistently meet the primary efficacy endpoint ... the majority did not' reach non-inferiority with PERT; sponsor blames enteric-capsule formulation. Should be the dated tier-5 contra entry (or move the efficacy contra to 2021).
Sponsor's 25 Sep 2019 OPTION release (10-K R7): ~50% of patients reached non-inferiority CFA; sponsor called it positive. A low-confidence tier-5 point the draft cites only in its judgement.
Phase 2 MS1819 + PERT combination trial in CF with severe EPI (BioSpace topline: CFA +6.57% from baseline). This is add-on use, not the minipig's monotherapy prediction; could go in patient_trials.

The in-vitro test-meal assay (Aloulou 2015: 10 mg YLLIP2 = 1200 mg pancreatin) is a separate system with its own prediction; the draft folds it into the minipig model_id in the dose cell. No patient comparison, so it would be an untested track at most.
No public disease-model data found for burlulipase or SLV339 (searches returned nothing), which agrees with the draft.

Burlulipase follow-on: Heubi 2016 called for 'a larger phase 2 dose ranging trial'; Anthera 10-K 2017 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1316175/000121465917002018/d3917010k.htm) lists NM-BL only as completed phase 1/2. No later burlulipase patient result found, so the canine track has no further comparison.
rule_questions: For an enzyme replacement, the model's PD readout (CFA) is also the efficacy endpoint. Can an uncontrolled CFA change from baseline in a safety-primary phase 2a be scored as engagement (readout_tier downstream) while the controlled CFA comparison is scored as efficacy? Or does that count one readout twice?

OPTION 2's sponsor puts the failure down to enteric-capsule formulation, which the minipig (purified enzyme) never tested. The brief would make an OPTION 2-only pairing untested. Does the non-enteric OPTION shortfall (55.6 vs 86.2) keep the contra by itself? I judged that it does.

Minipigs got milligram doses of purified YLLIP2; patients got grams of MS1819-SD spray-dried powder with undisclosed lipase content. When the dose cell is untested (no_prediction), can an under-dose explanation ever move efficacy to untested, or does efficacy always follow the trial?

Efficacy 2 dating: AzurRx's 25 Sep 2019 OPTION release (sponsor 'positive'; ~50% of patients reached non-inferiority, no group CFA means) was public earlier than the 31 Mar 2021 OPTION 2 topline. Does a half-of-patients shortfall framed as positive count as the earliest public contra comparison under rule 6/7? I kept 2021.
